title: Coherence of normalized affine sections square comparisons
statement: Let $R,B$ be commutative rings, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme], with fibre-product projections $p:X\prime\to X$, $f\prime:X\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the fixed derived categories, derived functors and affine sections [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-affine-global-hom-base-change-map]. Supply $t,b,z,d,v,r$ with the identity-on-sections and derived-unit normalizations of [lem-pc-affine-sections-composition-comparisons], and supply $s:p_*;\Gamma_f\cong\Gamma_{f\prime};\rho$ and $c:Rp_*;R\Gamma_f\cong R\Gamma_{f\prime};D\rho$, where $s$ is identity on sections and $c$ obeys the corresponding right-derived-unit normalization displayed in lean.statement. Put $k=(c_{f\prime,g});L(f\prime g=pf);(c_{p,f})^{-1}:Lg^*;Lf\prime^*\cong Lf^*;Lp^*$, using the fixed comparisons of [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. Let $\delta:Rp_*;Rf_*\to Rf\prime_*;Rg_*$ be the conjugate of $k$ under the pinned composite pullback/direct-image adjunctions. For every $F\in D(\mathcal O_{X\prime})$, $R\Gamma_R(\delta_F);r_{Rf\prime_*F};D\rho(d_F)=b_{Rp_*F};c_F$. This is composition coherence only: no base-change map, pullback unit, quasi-coherence or flatness occurs.

proof.text: For the fibre-product square form k: Lg*;Lf' * ≅ Lf*;Lp* by the fixed derived-pullback composition comparisons and pullback.condition. Let δ: Rp*;Rf* → Rf' *;Rg* be its conjugate under the pinned composite adjunctions. The normalized derived-adjunction Hom-equivalence equation and the left-derived characterization of the composition comparisons identify δ with the right-derived map induced by the identity-on-sections underived pushforward square.

Choose a K-injective representative J of F. Direct-image and direct-image/global-sections acyclicity, followed by exact restriction of scalars, make the pasted unit of p_*;f_*;Γ_R at J invertible. Precompose both sides with this unit. Use the pinned unit equation for δ, then hb,hc on the p,f path and hr,hd on the f',g path. Naturality of derived units and the exact-restriction comparison equations reduce the two sides to localization of the two underived sections comparisons.

The underived composites are equal on every section because ht,hz,hv,hs make each comparison the identity on elements; the fibre-product condition identifies their scalar actions. Cancel the invertible pasted unit at J. Every F is isomorphic to a localized K-injective representative, so naturality of all comparisons transports the identity to every F. Identity squares give the composition unit law and F=0 gives equality of zero maps.
